claims.text: Nearly equiatomic FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt alloys possess an FCC structure.
Nearly equiatomic FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt alloys have high saturation magnetization.
Nearly equiatomic FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit low coercivity or soft ferromagnetism.
A low concentration of carbon can be incorporated interstitially into the FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt matrix during methane-containing reactive-gas synthesis.
Interstitial carbon will create localized lattice distortion in the FCC matrix.
The carbon-induced distortion will take the form of subtle tetragonal strain.
Carbon-induced lattice distortion will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Interstitial carbon and its associated lattice distortion will enhance domain-wall pinning.
Greater magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will raise the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The increased barrier to domain-wall motion will increase coercivity.
Low-level carbon doping will increase coercivity by at least 50% relative to an undoped FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt baseline.
The carbon-doped alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The carbon-doped alloy will retain an FCC structure.
The beneficial coercivity effect is limited to carbon concentrations low enough to avoid carbide formation and phase segregation.
Near-equiatomic composition and configurational entropy above 1.0R can be maintained after carbon incorporation.
The optimal carbon concentration and its effect on microstructural stability and magnetic properties are uncertain and processing-dependent.
XRD and TEM can be used to test FCC phase retention, carbide formation, and the proposed lattice strain.
Room-temperature magnetic hysteresis measurements can compare coercive field and saturation magnetization between doped and undoped samples.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires a controlled methane-containing reactive-gas atmosphere, whereas the boundary refers to 'standard ambient synthesis' conditions. It is unclear whether ambient synthesis is intended to include or exclude the specified reactive atmosphere.
